mainTopic: Errors and concentration in קריאת שמע, workers' obligations in prayer and ברכות, and the exemption of a חתן and one busy with a מצוה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a דרשה: אהלים (tents of Torah) sit next to נחלים (streams) in a פסוק, teaching that Torah study lifts a person from guilt to merit. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about mistakes in קריאת שמע. On his wedding day, רבי אלעזר hears a ברייתא and a limit from רבי יוחנן about where to go back when you don't know where you erred. A new משנה follows. Workers may say שמע up a tree but not תפילה, and a חתן is exempt from שמע, though רבן גמליאל recited it anyway so as not to give up מלכות שמים. The גמרא asks how workers can have כוונה. It answers that they must stop working for the first section of שמע. It then sorts out when workers pray a full or shortened שמונה עשרה and bless after eating, depending on whether they are paid wages or only a meal. Finally, it brings the פסוק source for the exemption of someone busy with a מצוה, read from the word 'your' in בשבתך ובלכתך.

steps.title: Why tents are placed next to streams in the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the closeness of 'tents' and 'streams' in a פסוק. Just as streams purify a person, tents of Torah lift a person from guilt to merit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Tents are placed next to streams, as it is written: 'Like streams stretched out, like gardens by the river, like tents planted…' This tells you: just as streams lift a person from impurity to purity, so too tents (of Torah) lift a person from the side of guilt to the side of merit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering a question on the previous amud: why does the פסוק put 'tents' right next to 'streams'? The answer is a lesson about the power of Torah study.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Streams can serve as a מקוה, so they purify someone who is טמא. 'Tents' here means the tents of Torah, the places where people learn. The פסוק pairs them to teach that learning Torah 'purifies' a person spiritually, moving him from כף חובה to כף זכות.

keyTerms.meaning: Tents; here read as the tents of Torah study
Streams; flowing water that can purify like a מקוה
Ritual impurity and purity
The scale (pan) of guilt
The scale (pan) of merit

steps.confusionAlert: In the פסוק, the word כַּאֲהָלִים (vowelled with a חטף פתח, 'ahalim') actually means aloes, a kind of fragrant tree. The גמרא reads it as אֹהָלִים, 'tents', to make the דרשה. Don't be thrown off if a חומש translation says 'aloes.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the aggadic section before the גמרא returns to the הלכות of קריאת שמע. It shows how highly the גמרא values Torah study.

phrases.english: Tents next to streams,
phrases.notes: Continues a question from the previous daf: why are these placed side by side?

phrases.english: as it is written:
"Like streams stretched out, like gardens by the river,
phrases.notes: במדבר כד:ו, from בלעם's blessing

phrases.english: like tents (aloes) planted, etc."
phrases.notes: Read by the גמרא as אֹהָלִים, tents

phrases.english: to tell you:
just as streams raise a person
from impurity to purity
phrases.notes: By immersing in them

phrases.english: so too tents raise a person
phrases.notes: Tents of Torah study

phrases.english: from the scale of guilt to the scale of merit.

steps.triggerLanguage: לוֹמַר לְךָ: מָה נְחָלִים מַעֲלִין אֶת הָאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question (from the preceding daf) of why tents and streams are placed next to each other
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Like streams that purify, Torah study lifts a person from guilt to merit
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Learning Torah moves a person from כף חובה to כף זכות

steps.title: Quoting the משנה on reading שמע out of order
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה: one who reads שמע out of order has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: "One who reads it backwards (out of order) has not fulfilled his obligation, etc."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה to start a new topic. This is a setup line: the discussion that follows connects to the end of this משנה, about someone who made a mistake while reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full משנה says that reading out of order does not count, and that someone who erred goes back to the place of his mistake. The וכו׳ ('etc.') points to that second part. The coming story and ברייתא deal with a case the משנה did not cover: what if he doesn't know where he erred?

keyTerms.meaning: Out of order, backwards
Did not fulfill his obligation
Etc.; the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: "One who reads (Shema) out of order
has not fulfilled his obligation, etc."
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: one who erred goes back to where he erred

steps.triggerLanguage: הַקּוֹרֵא לְמַפְרֵעַ לֹא יָצָא וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadah and returns to the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reading שמע out of order does not count; one who errs must go back to the point of error

steps.title: רבי אלעזר goes to the בית מדרש during his wedding preparations
steps.stepSummary: While רבי אמי and רבי אסי tie the חופה for רבי אלעזר, he goes to the בית מדרש. There he finds a תנא reciting a teaching before רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי אסי were tying the wedding canopy for רבי אלעזר. He said to them: 'In the meantime, I will go and hear something in the study hall, and I will come back and tell it to you.' He went and found the תנא who was reciting before רבי יוחנן:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story to introduce the ברייתא that comes next. This step sets up the teaching; the actual halacha is in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows how dear Torah was to רבי אלעזר: even on his wedding day he used spare time to learn. It also tells us the source of the coming ברייתא: a תנא recited it in front of רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Wedding canopy (חופה)
In the meantime
The study hall
Here: a reciter who memorized ברייתות and recited them in the study hall

steps.confusionAlert: Here תנא does not mean a sage of the משנה period. It means a professional reciter who memorized ברייתות and recited them before the sages.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi

phrases.aramaic: הֲווֹ קָא קָטְרִין לֵיהּ גְּנָנָא לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר.
phrases.english: were tying the wedding canopy for Rabbi Elazar.
He said to them: In the meantime,
I will go and hear something in the study hall,
and I will come back and tell it to you.
He went and found the reciter
who was reciting before Rabbi Yochanan:

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי הֲווֹ קָא קָטְרִין לֵיהּ גְּנָנָא לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrative frame that introduces a ברייתא expanding on the משנה's rule about errors

steps.title: Where to go back to when you don't know where you erred in שמע
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא: if someone erred and doesn't know where, the answer depends on where he is now. Mid-paragraph, go back to the start of the paragraph. Between paragraphs, go back to the first paragraph break. Between the two 'וכתבתם' verses, go back to the first one.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who read שמע and made a mistake, and doesn't know where he made it: if he is in the middle of a paragraph, he goes back to the beginning of it. If he is between paragraphs, he goes back to the first paragraph break. If he is between one 'writing' verse and the other, he goes back to the first 'writing' verse.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the teaching רבי אלעזר heard. It handles a case the משנה left open: what to do when you know you made a mistake but don't know exactly where.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said to go back to the place of the error, but here the place is unknown. So the rule is to go back to the earliest possible point, to be sure nothing is skipped. The 'כתיבה' case covers the confusion caused by the nearly identical פסוק 'וכתבתם על מזזות ביתך ובשעריך', which appears in both שמע and והיה אם שמוע.

keyTerms.meaning: He read and made a mistake
Here: a paragraph of שמע, not a chapter
He must go back to the beginning
'Writing': the פסוק 'וכתבתם' that appears in two paragraphs

steps.confusionAlert: 'בין כתיבה לכתיבה' does not mean between written lines. It refers to the two identical פסוקים of 'וכתבתם על מזזות ביתך', one in the first paragraph and one in the second. Because they are identical, a person can lose track of which one he just said.
steps.whatToRemember: When unsure where you erred in שמע, go back to the earliest point you could have been at: the start of the paragraph, the first paragraph break, or the first 'וכתבתם.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets practical halacha for anyone who loses focus during קריאת שמע. It also teaches a general approach: when in doubt, go back far enough to be sure.

phrases.english: One who read (Shema) and erred
and does not know where he erred:
if in the middle of a paragraph, he goes back to its beginning.
phrases.notes: פרק means a paragraph of שמע

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין פֶּרֶק לְפֶרֶק — יַחְזוֹר לְפֶרֶק רִאשׁוֹן.
phrases.english: If between paragraphs, he goes back to the first paragraph break.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין כְּתִיבָה לִכְתִיבָה — יַחְזוֹר לִכְתִיבָה רִאשׁוֹנָה.
phrases.english: If between one 'writing' and the other, he goes back to the first 'writing.'
phrases.notes: The two 'וכתבתם' verses (דברים ו:ט and יא:כ)

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרָא וְטָעָה וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ לְהֵיכָן טָעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The content of the teaching רבי אלעזר heard, introduced by the story in the previous step
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the place of error is unknown, return to the earliest possible point: start of the paragraph, first paragraph break, or first 'וכתבתם'

steps.title: רבי יוחנן limits the case of the two 'וכתבתם' verses
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the ruling 'go back to the first וכתבתם' only applies if the person had not yet started 'למען ירבו ימיכם'. If he had, we assume habit carried him through correctly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: They only taught this when he had not yet started 'למען ירבו ימיכם'. But if he did start 'למען ירבו ימיכם', he followed his usual routine and kept going.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן responds to the ברייתא the תנא just recited. He narrows its last case, about someone who got confused between the two 'וכתבתם' verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וכתבתם' appears twice: once at the end of the first paragraph (ואהבת) and once at the end of the second paragraph (והיה אם שמע). Someone who is unsure which one he just said should go back to the first one. רבי יוחנן adds a limit: if he already reached 'למען ירבו ימיכם', which comes only after the second one, he must have been on the right track, so he does not go back.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this when… (a phrase that limits a rule)
He began
'So that your days may be lengthened', the verse right after the second וכתבתם
He followed his routine and kept going (habit kept him on track)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not arguing with the ברייתא. He is only limiting when its last case applies.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a key idea: when someone has clearly moved past the confusing spot, we trust that habit carried him through correctly.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to him:
They only taught this
where he had not yet begun 'In order to lengthen your days'
but if he had begun 'In order to lengthen your days',
he followed his routine and continued (correctly).
phrases.notes: We assume he said the second וכתבתם, since 'למען ירבו' follows it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא פָּתַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the last case of the ברייתא from Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he already started 'למען ירבו ימיכם', he does not go back. Habit kept him on track.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר reports back, and the rabbis praise the teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר returns and tells רבי אמי and רבי אסי what he heard. They say it alone would have been worth coming for.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came and told them. They said to him: If we had come only to hear this, it would have been enough for us.
steps.whatsHappening: The story from Step 3 wraps up. רבי אלעזר brings רבי יוחנן's teaching back to the wedding, and the rabbis express how much they value it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the story and also closes the גמרא's discussion of the mistakes in שמע. The rabbis' praise shows how valued רבי יוחנן's limit was. It settles a common doubt in everyday practice.

keyTerms.meaning: If only / had it been that
It would have been enough for us

steps.whatToRemember: Someone unsure of his place in שמע goes back based on where he is now. But if he already reached 'למען ירבו ימיכם', he relies on habit and keeps going.

phrases.english: He came and told them.
They said to him:
Had we not come
except to hear this matter,
it would have been sufficient for us.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִלּוּ לֹא בָּאנוּ אֶלָּא לִשְׁמוֹעַ דָּבָר זֶה דַּיֵּינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story by reporting רבי יוחנן's teaching back to the rabbis.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן's limit on the ברייתא is accepted and highly valued.

steps.title: New משנה: laborers may recite שמע at their work spot
steps.stepSummary: Workers may say שמע while up a tree or on top of a wall they are building. They may not do this for תפילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Workers may recite שמע at the top of a tree or at the top of a row of stones. They are not allowed to do this for תפילה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins here. It teaches that laborers do not have to come down from their work to say שמע, but they do have to come down for תפילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is about concentration. שמע can be said with enough focus even in an uncomfortable spot. תפילה (the עמידה) needs much deeper focus of the heart, so a worker cannot say it while balanced on a tree or a wall.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marked here as מַתְנִי׳)
Craftsmen / hired laborers
A row of stones in a wall being built
The עמידה prayer

steps.confusionAlert: Calling שמע 'easier' does not mean it needs no focus. It only needs less concentration than תפילה.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Laborers
may recite (שמע) at the top of the tree
and at the top of the row of stones.

phrases.aramaic: מַה שֶּׁאֵינָן רַשָּׁאִין לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן בַּתְּפִלָּה.
phrases.english: which they are not permitted to do for תפילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוּמָּנִין קוֹרִין בְּרֹאשׁ הָאִילָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about how much concentration שמע requires.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Laborers may say שמע at their work spot, but not תפילה.

steps.title: A חתן is exempt from קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: A groom is exempt from שמע from the first night until מוצאי שבת, as long as the marriage has not yet been consummated.
steps.simpleTranslation: A groom is exempt from reciting שמע on the first night, and until Saturday night, if he has not done the act.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second rule. A new חתן does not have to say שמע for the first few nights of his marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is that his mind is too preoccupied to focus properly on שמע. The exemption ends once the marriage is consummated, because the worry is gone. This connects to Step 7's theme: שמע needs at least some real concentration.

keyTerms.meaning: A groom
Exempt
Saturday night, after שבת ends
Did the act (consummated the marriage)

phrases.english: A groom is exempt from the recitation of שמע
on the first night
and until Saturday night,
if he has not done the act (consummated the marriage).

steps.triggerLanguage: חָתָן פָּטוּר מִקְּרִיאַת שְׁמַע לַיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second rule in the same משנה, also tied to concentration in שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חתן is exempt from שמע until מוצאי שבת if the marriage was not yet consummated.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל recites שמע on his wedding night, and his students question him
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל said שמע on his first night of marriage. His students challenged him with his own teaching that a חתן is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story with רבן גמליאל: he married a woman and recited שמע on the first night. His students said to him: Didn't you, our teacher, teach us that a groom is exempt from שמע?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells a story that seems to clash with the rule it just taught. The students point out the conflict, which sets up רבן גמליאל's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The students are not really asking for information. They are challenging his behavior using his own teaching. If he is exempt, why is he saying it?

keyTerms.meaning: An incident / a story that happened
The נשיא (head of the Sanhedrin)
His students

phrases.english: And there was an incident with רבן גמליאל
who married a woman
and recited (שמע) on the first night.
His students said to him:
Did you, our teacher, not teach us
that a groom is exempt from the recitation of שמע?

steps.triggerLanguage: לִמַּדְתָּנוּ רַבֵּינוּ שֶׁחָתָן פָּטוּר מִקְּרִיאַת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story in which רבן גמליאל seems to act against the rule of Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's choice to say שמע on his wedding night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He himself taught that a חתן is exempt, so his reciting seems to contradict his own teaching.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל will not give up accepting Heaven's Kingdom even for a moment
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל answers that he refuses to remove the acceptance of מלכות שמים from himself, even for one moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I will not listen to you and remove from myself the Kingdom of Heaven, even for one moment.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל answers his students. He explains that he chose to say שמע even though he was exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not deny the exemption. He chooses to go beyond it. For him, saying שמע means accepting עול מלכות שמים, and he did not want to be without that even briefly. The rule of Step 8 stays in place, and רבן גמליאל's conduct is a personal exception.

keyTerms.meaning: I will not listen to you
The Kingdom of Heaven (accepting God as King)
Even one moment

steps.whatToRemember: A חתן is exempt from שמע, but רבן גמליאל chose to say it anyway so he would not go even a moment without accepting מלכות שמים.
steps.confusionAlert: רבן גמליאל is not cancelling the exemption for a חתן. The rule still stands. He chose to go beyond it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story is the basis for the later גמרא discussion of whether someone who is exempt may choose to recite שמע anyway.

phrases.english: He said to them:
I will not listen to you
to remove from myself the Kingdom of Heaven
even for one moment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינִי שׁוֹמֵעַ לָכֶם לְבַטֵּל הֵימֶנִי מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' challenge from Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבן גמליאל recited שמע even though a חתן is exempt.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He chose not to give up accepting מלכות שמים even for a moment.

steps.title: Workers may say שמע up a tree, but תפילה depends on the tree
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that workers may say קריאת שמע at the top of a tree or a wall. They may say תפילה only atop an olive or fig tree, and they must climb down from other trees. A בעל הבית must always climb down to pray.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The חכמים taught: Workers say שמע at the top of a tree or at the top of a row of stones. They may pray at the top of an olive tree or a fig tree. From all other trees, they climb down and pray. A homeowner climbs down and prays in every case, because his mind is not settled up there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that adds details to the משנה's rule about workers. It explains when workers may say תפילה in a tree, which the משנה did not discuss in detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמע is allowed anywhere up high, but תפילה needs more focus. Olive and fig trees have many close branches, so a worker can stand steady and concentrate. A בעל הבית works for himself and can take the time to climb down, so the חכמים never allowed him to pray up in a tree.

keyTerms.meaning: Hired workers or laborers
A row of stones in a wall being built
A homeowner who works for himself
His mind is settled, so he can focus

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two מצוות. In this ברייתא, workers may say שמע in any tree, but תפילה is limited to olive and fig trees.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
Workers recite [Shema] at the top of the tree
and at the top of the row of stones.
And they pray at the top of the olive tree
and at the top of the fig tree.
But all the other trees —
they climb down and pray.
phrases.notes: Other trees have spread-out branches, so the worker cannot stand steady and focus.

phrases.aramaic: וּבַעַל הַבַּיִת, בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ
phrases.english: And the homeowner, in either case,
climbs down and prays,
because his mind is not settled upon him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָאוּמָּנִין קוֹרִין בְּרֹאשׁ הָאִילָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the משנה's rule about workers (step 7) with a ברייתא that adds details about תפילה and the בעל הבית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Workers may say שמע anywhere up high. They may pray only atop an olive or fig tree. A בעל הבית must always climb down to pray.

steps.title: Does שמע require כוונה or not?
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי points out a contradiction to רבא. The משנה lets workers say שמע up a tree, which suggests no כוונה is needed. But a ברייתא learns from a גזירה שוה that שמע does require כוונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי, the son of שמואל's daughter, raised a contradiction to רבא. We learned that workers say שמע at the top of a tree or a wall, so it seems no focus is needed. But a ברייתא says that whoever reads שמע must focus his heart. It says 'שמע ישראל,' and later it says 'הסכת ושמע ישראל.' Just as there it means paying attention, so too here it means paying attention.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי sets two sources against each other. One seems to say שמע needs no focus, while the other says it clearly does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing on a tree or a wall is shaky, so the חכמים assume a person cannot focus well there. If the משנה still allows שמע there, it seems כוונה is not required. The ברייתא, however, uses the shared word 'שמע' in both פסוקים to prove that שמע requires 'הסכת', meaning full attention.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a contradiction between two sources
Focus or concentration of the heart
And they contrasted it with another source
Pay attention, listen carefully
Evidently, it follows that

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key question of the whole passage: how can workers say שמע properly while they are distracted by their job?

phrases.english: Rav Mari raised a contradiction
son of the daughter of Shmuel, to Rava:
We learned: Workers recite [Shema]
at the top of the tree and at the top of the row of stones,
evidently it does not require focus.
And he contrasted it [with a ברייתא]:
One who reads Shema
must focus his heart,
as it says: "Hear, Israel,"
and further on it says:
"Pay attention and hear, Israel."
phrases.notes: דברים כז:ט

phrases.english: Just as there it is with attention,
so too here it is with attention.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב מָרִי בְּרַהּ דְּבַת שְׁמוּאֵל לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the workers' rule from steps 7 and 11 by pairing it with a ברייתא that requires כוונה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that workers may say שמע up a tree or a wall.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If workers may say שמע in a place where they cannot focus, then כוונה is not required. That contradicts the גזירה שוה from 'הסכת', which requires כוונה for שמע.

steps.title: רבא is silent and asks what רב מרי has heard
steps.stepSummary: רבא has no answer to the contradiction, so he stays silent. He then asks רב מרי whether he has heard any teaching on this question.
steps.simpleTranslation: He [רבא] was silent. He said to him: Have you heard anything about this?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא cannot resolve the contradiction, so he asks רב מרי for a tradition. This step sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is resolved yet. The step shows that the contradiction is strong enough to leave רבא without an answer, and it moves the discussion to a received teaching instead of new reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: He was silent
Have you heard anything?

phrases.english: He [Rava] was silent.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִידֵּי שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ בְּהָא?
phrases.english: He said to him: Have you heard anything on this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִשְׁתִּיק. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִידֵּי שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ בְּהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the contradiction in step 12. רבא has no answer and asks for a tradition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב מרי knows a teaching that resolves the contradiction about כוונה.

steps.title: רב ששת: workers must stop working to say שמע
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי quotes רב ששת. The משנה's permission applies only when the workers stop their work while they say שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רב ששת said: The rule applies only when they stop their work and recite.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי answers the contradiction with a teaching from רב ששת. The workers may stay up in the tree, but they must pause their work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this answer, the משנה never meant that שמע needs no כוונה. Being up high is not what disturbs focus; working is. Once they stop working, they can concentrate even while standing in the tree.

keyTerms.meaning: They stop their work
And this applies only when

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת —
phrases.english: He said to him: Thus said Rav Sheshet:
And this is when they stop their work and recite.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת וְהוּא שֶׁבְּטֵלִין מִמְּלַאכְתָּן וְקוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 13 and resolves the contradiction from step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the משנה refers only to workers who stop working.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Workers may say שמע while working up a tree, which suggests no כוונה is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Workers say שמע in the tree only after stopping their work, so they can have כוונה.

steps.title: Challenge from בית הלל: workers keep working while reciting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ששת. A ברייתא says that according to בית הלל, workers keep doing their work while they say שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: But was it not taught: בית הלל say that they keep busy with their work and recite!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב ששת's answer with a ברייתא that seems to say the exact opposite. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת said workers must stop working, but this ברייתא quotes בית הלל, whose opinion is the הלכה, saying workers do not stop. That brings back the original problem of how workers can have כוונה while they work.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught in a ברייתא? (used to open a challenge)
The school of הלל
They keep busy with their work

phrases.english: But was it not taught:
Beit Hillel say:
They engage in their work and recite!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים עוֹסְקִים בִּמְלַאכְתָּן וְקוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב ששת's answer from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that workers must stop working to say שמע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא quotes בית הלל saying workers keep working while they recite. That directly contradicts the requirement to stop working.

steps.title: Stopping work depends on which part of שמע
steps.stepSummary: Workers must stop working for the first section of שמע, but may keep working during the second section.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this source speaks about the first section, and that source speaks about the second section.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the last step. Both sources are true, but each one speaks about a different part of שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת's rule that workers stop working applies to the first section of שמע, which needs full כוונה. The ברייתא of בית הלל, which lets them keep working, applies to the later section. So the contradiction disappears, and the earlier idea that שמע needs כוונה stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources do not really clash
The first section of שמע, which needs full focus
The second section of שמע

steps.confusionAlert: Here פרק does not mean a chapter of the גמרא or משנה. It means a section of קריאת שמע itself.
steps.whatToRemember: Workers must stop working for the first section of שמע because it needs כוונה. They may keep working for the rest.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this refers to the first section,
phrases.notes: This is רב ששת's rule that workers stop working.

phrases.english: that refers to the second section.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא of בית הלל, which lets them keep working.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּפֶרֶק רִאשׁוֹן, הָא בְּפֶרֶק שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15 against רב ששת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different section of שמע
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ששת seemed to require stopping work for all of שמע, which contradicts the ברייתא
steps.terutzMaskana: Workers stop only for the first section, so both sources stand

steps.title: What workers must still do while employed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the מצוות workers still do on the job, along with the communal roles they skip.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: Workers doing a job for an employer read שמע and say its ברכות before and after. They eat their bread and say ברכות before and after it. They also pray the full שמונה עשרה. But they do not go down before the ark to lead the prayers, and they do not do ברכת כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about workers. It sets out what they must do and what they skip because they are on their employer's time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Workers keep all their personal obligations, including the full שמונה עשרה. They give up only extra communal roles, like being שליח ציבור or doing נשיאת כפים, because those would take time away from their employer. The words 'full שמונה עשרה' will be challenged in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; this introduces a ברייתא
Hired workers
Going down before the ark, meaning leading the prayers as שליח ציבור
Lifting their hands, meaning doing ברכת כהנים

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the balance between a worker's duty to his employer and his own מצוות. The worker keeps his core obligations but skips the extras.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Workers who were doing work
for an employer,
recite the Shema
and say the blessings before it and after it.
And they eat their bread
and say the blessings before it and after it,
and they pray the prayer of eighteen blessings.
phrases.notes: This means the full עמידה.

phrases.english: But they do not go down before the ark to lead,
and they do not lift their hands for the Priestly Blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַפּוֹעֲלִים שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹשִׂין מְלָאכָה אֵצֶל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about the obligations of workers
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Workers say שמע with its ברכות, say ברכות on their bread, and pray the full שמונה עשרה. They do not lead the prayers or do ברכת כהנים.

steps.title: Another ברייתא allows workers a shortened prayer
steps.stepSummary: A different ברייתא says workers pray only a shortened version of שמונה עשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in another ברייתא that workers pray a shortened version of the eighteen blessings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא it just brought. Another ברייתא gives workers only a short summary prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא requires the full שמונה עשרה. The second allows only מעין שמונה עשרה, a short version that sums up the blessings. Both cannot be the rule for workers.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא; this introduces a contradicting source
A shortened version of the עמידה that sums up the eighteen blessings

phrases.english: But it was taught: a shortened form of the eighteen blessings!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא מֵעֵין שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that workers pray the full שמונה עשרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Contradiction between two ברייתות about the same case

steps.title: The two ברייתות follow two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says one ברייתא follows רבן גמליאל and the other follows רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: It is not difficult. This ברייתא follows רבן גמליאל, and that ברייתא follows רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the contradiction. Each ברייתא follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל holds that a person must always pray the full eighteen blessings, so workers do too. רבי יהושע allows a shortened prayer, so the second ברייתא follows his view. The two sources simply reflect a known disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who requires the full שמונה עשרה every day
The תנא who allows מעין שמונה עשרה

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
It is not difficult,
this one follows Rabban Gamliel,
phrases.notes: This is the full שמונה עשרה.

phrases.english: that one follows Rabbi Yehoshua.
phrases.notes: This is the shortened prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, הָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each ברייתא to a different תנא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to give one rule for workers
steps.terutzMaskana: Each ברייתא reflects a different תנא's view on the required length of prayer

steps.title: Why mention workers if anyone may shorten?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא singles out workers, since רבי יהושע lets anyone shorten.
steps.simpleTranslation: If this ברייתא follows רבי יהושע, why does it speak about workers? Even any person may also pray the shortened version!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב ששת's answer. If the shortened prayer follows רבי יהושע, there is no reason to mention workers in particular.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא presents the shortened prayer as a special allowance for workers. But רבי יהושע allows every person to pray that way. So the detail about workers seems pointless if the ברייתא follows him.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this case? This asks why a source singles something out
Even any person also

phrases.english: If it follows Rabbi Yehoshua,
why speak specifically of workers?
Even any person may also do so!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, מַאי אִירְיָא פּוֹעֲלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's answer in step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that the shortened-prayer ברייתא follows רבי יהושע
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's focus on workers would be pointless under רבי יהושע, who allows everyone to shorten

steps.title: Both teachings follow רבן גמליאל: wage-workers versus meal-workers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the רבי יהושע answer. It says both ברייתות follow רבן גמליאל, but they describe different kinds of workers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both ברייתות follow רבן גמליאל, and there is no contradiction. The one that lets workers shorten their prayer is about workers who are paid wages. The one that requires the full prayer is about workers who are paid only with their meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The question in Step 20 was why a ברייתא would single out workers if, according to רבי יהושע, anyone may shorten. So the גמרא now gives a brand-new answer: both ברייתות agree with רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A worker paid wages owes his employer his time, so he may shorten שמונה עשרה. A worker paid only with food is basically doing a favor, so he owes less of his time and must pray the full version. The difference between the ברייתות is now about the type of worker, not about which תנא they follow.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, meaning both sources
And it is not difficult; there is no contradiction
For their wages (paid workers)
For their meal (paid only with food)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the wage-worker versus meal-worker split. The rest of the section depends on that split.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. The wage-worker is the one who prays the SHORT version. The meal-worker prays the FULL version.

phrases.english: Rather, both this one and that one follow Rabban Gamliel,
phrases.notes: אלא signals that the earlier answer is being replaced.

phrases.english: and it is not difficult:
here, it is about those who work for their wages.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that allows a shortened prayer.

phrases.english: here, it is about those who work for their meal.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that requires the full prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 20 by replacing רב ששת's answer with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): the two sources describe different kinds of workers.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות disagree because they follow different תנאים (רבן גמליאל vs. רבי יהושע).
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow רבן גמליאל. Wage-workers shorten, and meal-workers pray in full.

steps.title: A teaching on how workers bless after eating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that workers shorten ברכת המזון to two ברכות. The key distinction comes in the next step.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: workers doing a job for a homeowner say קריאת שמע and pray. When they eat their bread, they do not make the ברכה before it, but they say two ברכות after it. How? The first ברכה is said as usual. For the second, he starts with ברכת הארץ and includes בונה ירושלים inside it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא to support its new answer. This part sets up the proof, which comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Workers save their employer's time by skipping the ברכה before eating. They also merge the third ברכה of ברכת המזון (בונה ירושלים) into the second (ברכת הארץ). This shows that חז"ל shortened workers' ברכות out of fairness to the employer.

keyTerms.meaning: And indeed it was taught (introduces a supporting ברייתא)
The homeowner / employer
The second ברכה of ברכת המזון, thanking for the land
The third ברכה of ברכת המזון, about rebuilding ירושלים
In its standard, established form

phrases.english: And indeed it was taught:
Laborers who were doing work
for the homeowner —
recite Shema and pray.
And they eat their bread —
and they do not bless before it,
phrases.notes: The ברכה before food is only rabbinic.

phrases.english: but they bless after it two blessings.
phrases.notes: ברכת המזון is from the Torah, so it is not skipped entirely.

phrases.english: How so?
The first blessing is said in its standard form,
for the second, he begins with the blessing of the land
and they include "Who builds Jerusalem" within the blessing of the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support the distinction made in Step 21.
steps.raayaObject: The distinction between wage-workers and meal-workers.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about workers' ברכות over food.

steps.title: The same teaching distinguishes wage-workers from meal-workers
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the shortened ברכת המזון to wage-workers. Meal-workers, or workers eating with the homeowner, bless in full. This proves Step 21's distinction.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does this apply? Only to workers paid wages. But workers paid with their meal, or workers whose employer is eating with them, say the ברכות in the full, standard way.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the heart of the proof. The ברייתא itself draws the exact line that the גמרא used in Step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא openly treats wage-workers and meal-workers differently, so that split is a real halachic category. If the split applies to ברכת המזון, it can also explain the two ברייתות about prayer. When the homeowner eats with them, he is clearly not in a rush, so there is no reason to shorten.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? (limits a ruling)
Reclining (eating) together with them

steps.whatToRemember: Wage-workers save their employer's time by shortening prayer and ברכת המזון. Meal-workers, or workers eating with the employer, say everything in full.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said? —
with those who work for their wages,
but those who work for their meal

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בַּעַל הַבַּיִת מֵיסֵב עִמָּהֶן —
phrases.english: or if the homeowner was reclining with them —
they bless in its standard form.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים — בְּעוֹשִׂין בִּשְׂכָרָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in Step 22 with the clause that proves the point.
steps.raayaObject: The wage-worker versus meal-worker distinction from Step 21.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The limiting clause of the ברייתא about ברכת המזון.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: a חתן is exempt from שמע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a חתן is exempt from קריאת שמע. This opens a new topic.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a groom is exempt from reciting קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. This sets up the search for its source in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the topic was workers. Now the גמרא turns to the חתן, who is exempt from קריאת שמע on his wedding night. The next step will show where this exemption comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: A groom
Exempt

phrases.english: A groom is exempt from the recitation of Shema.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָתָן פָּטוּר מִקְּרִיאַת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חתן is exempt from קריאת שמע.

steps.title: The פסוק that exempts someone busy with a מצוה and a חתן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the words of the פסוק to exclude someone busy with a מצוה, and a חתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: "When you sit in your house" excludes someone busy with a מצוה. "And when you walk on the way" excludes a חתן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the פסוק source for the חתן's exemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Your sitting" and "your walking" describe a person going about his own ordinary business. Someone busy with a מצוה is not in that state, so he is exempt. The חתן is also excluded, because he is preoccupied and worried about the מצוה of his wedding night.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
When you sit in your house (from the פסוק of שמע)
To the exclusion of; leaving out
One who is busy doing a מצוה

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"When you sit in your house" —
to the exclusion of one engaged in a מצוה.
"And when you walk on the way" —
to the exclusion of a groom.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ בְּבֵיתֶךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק source for the משנה's rule quoted in Step 24.
steps.raayaObject: The exemption of a חתן (and one busy with a מצוה) from קריאת שמע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words בשבתך בביתך ובלכתך בדרך in the פסוק of שמע.

steps.title: Marrying a virgin exempts, marrying a widow does not
steps.stepSummary: From the derivation, the ברייתא concludes that one who marries a בתולה is exempt, but one who marries an אלמנה is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: one who marries a virgin is exempt from קריאת שמע, but one who marries a widow is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא draws a practical conclusion from the פסוק it just explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption is based on the חתן being preoccupied and anxious. That anxiety applies when he marries a בתולה. When he marries an אלמנה there is no such worry, so the ordinary obligation stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: From here they said (a conclusion drawn from a source)
One who marries
A virgin bride
A widow
Obligated

steps.whatToRemember: A חתן is exempt from קריאת שמע because he is preoccupied with the מצוה of his wedding night. So the exemption applies only when he marries a בתולה, not an אלמנה.

phrases.english: From here they said:
One who marries a virgin is exempt,
but one who marries a widow is obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical rule from the derivation in Step 25.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The חתן's exemption applies only when he marries a בתולה. One who marries an אלמנה must say קריאת שמע.

steps.title: Where in the words is this exemption hinted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the words "בשבתך בביתך" show that someone busy with a מצוה is exempt, as the ברייתא claimed.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where is this implied?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the words of the פסוק show that someone busy with a מצוה is exempt from קריאת שמע. This question sets up רב פפא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the surface, "בשבתך בביתך" just describes when to say שמע: when you are at home. Nothing in it openly mentions an exemption for someone busy with a מצוה. So the גמרא wants to know what in the wording points to one.

keyTerms.meaning: What implies it? How do we see this in the words?
"And when you walk on the way" (the פסוק of קריאת שמע)

phrases.english: What implies it?
phrases.notes: Asking how the ברייתא's exemption is drawn from the פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the textual basis of the ברייתא's derivation in Step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which feature of the words "בשבתך בביתך" shows an exemption for someone busy with a מצוה.

steps.title: רב פפא: the trip in the פסוק is a voluntary one
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the פסוק describes a voluntary journey, so the obligation covers only people doing voluntary things.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: "Like a way." Just as a way (a trip) is voluntary, so too here it means voluntary activity.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that the "way" in the פסוק is an ordinary, optional trip. So the obligation of שמע is for people doing optional things, not for people busy with a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא compares "sitting in your house" to the "way" mentioned right after it in the פסוק. A trip on the road is normally רשות (optional), so the sitting must also describe a voluntary state. Someone busy with a מצוה is not in that state, so he is left out of the obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who explains the derivation
Optional or voluntary, not a מצוה
"Just as ... so too" (a comparison formula)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Like a way.
phrases.notes: The "way" in the פסוק is the model case.

phrases.english: Just as a way is voluntary,
so too here it is voluntary.
phrases.notes: Only voluntary activities fall under the obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כִּי דֶרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The "way" in the פסוק is voluntary, so the obligation applies only to voluntary activity, which leaves out someone busy with a מצוה.

steps.title: But the trip could be for a מצוה too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the פסוק could also be talking about someone traveling for a מצוה, and still the תורה says to read שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are we not dealing even with someone going to do a מצוה? And even so, the תורה said: let him read (שמע).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא: the word "way" does not prove the trip is optional. A person could be traveling to do a מצוה, and the פסוק still tells him to say שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is that "דרך" is a general word. It covers every kind of trip, including one for a מצוה. If so, the פסוק would obligate even someone busy with a מצוה, which is the opposite of the ברייתא's exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: Are we not dealing with...? (a challenge formula)
A מצוה matter or errand
"The Merciful One", meaning the תורה or ה׳

phrases.english: Are we not dealing
with one who is going for a מצוה matter,
and even so the Torah said: let him read (Shema).
phrases.notes: So the פסוק seems to obligate even someone on a מצוה trip.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי לָא עָסְקִינַן דְּקָאָזֵיל לִדְבַר מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's reading in Step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that the "way" in the פסוק must be voluntary.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: "דרך" is a general word that includes trips for a מצוה. So the פסוק could just as easily obligate someone busy with a מצוה.

steps.title: The word "your" limits it to personal walking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from the extra suffix in בלכתך ("your walking"): only your own personal travel obligates you, and travel for a מצוה is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the פסוק say "בלכת" (when walking). Why does it say "בלכתך" (when you walk)? Learn from this: it is your own walking that obligates you, but walking for a מצוה, you are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב פפא by pointing to the exact wording. The פסוק could have said "when walking" but said "when YOU walk", so it means your own personal business.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof moves from the meaning of "דרך" to the extra suffix ךָ ("your"). If the תורה meant every trip, the short form בלכת would have been enough. The added "your" limits the obligation to your private activity, so someone busy with a מצוה is exempt. This confirms the ברייתא of Step 25.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Let the פסוק say...
Learn from this; conclude from it
You are exempt

steps.whatToRemember: The words "בשבתך / בלכתך" stress "your". That teaches that the obligation of קריאת שמע applies when you are doing your own business. Someone busy with a מצוה (עוסק במצוה) is exempt.
steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not from the word "דרך" alone, which the קשיא already weakened. It comes from the extra suffix "ךָ" ("your") in בלכתך.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the principle that someone busy with a מצוה is exempt from קריאת שמע. The גמרא still needs to explain how the חתן's exemption follows from "ובלכתך בדרך", and it takes this up on the next amud.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say "when walking";
what is "when you walk"?
phrases.notes: Why add "your"?

phrases.english: Learn from this:
it is in your own walking that you are obligated,
but walking for a מצוה, you are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, לֵימָא קְרָא ״בְּלֶכֶת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 29 and confirms the exemption.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the wording (extra suffix)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "Way" is general, so even someone on a trip for a מצוה would be obligated.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra "your" limits the obligation to personal, voluntary activity. Someone busy with a מצוה is exempt.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only someone doing his own business is obligated in קריאת שמע. Someone busy with a מצוה is exempt.
